digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler bridge, inbound link applier
propositions: Reconciler re-derives and re-attempts the same structurally-impossible inbound Jira→rebar link writes every pass because failed ADD records are never durably recorded and the differ re-emits them from current local state alone.

Three deterministic structural verdicts (source closed, redundant ancestry, would create cycle) raised by graph/_links.py::add_dependency are caught, logged as WARNING, and retried identically next pass, creating a permanent ~19-line error floor and ~200+ doomed writes/hour.

Failed link writes are never memoized, so the applier has no memory of permanent impossibility and cannot skip a doomed write until the applier consults a durable record of attempted impossible links keyed on a deciding digest.

The deciding digest must cover the parent chain of each endpoint (not just the endpoint itself) because add_dependency calls resolve_hierarchy_link first, which may redirect to a type-tier ancestor before validation; cycle verdicts must include the global transitive graph to detect when an intermediate ticket change breaks the cycle.

The impossible_links.json store file must be committed to the tickets branch by the binding snapshot helper, or the record lives only in the working tree and is discarded between CI checkouts, leaving the bug unfixed in production despite passing unit tests.
